title: Homology of a constant matrix cone after exact slice restriction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a small site $(C,J)$, and the concrete data of [def-sp-integral-matrix-model-data]. Let $U\in C$, let $d:A^a\to A^b$ be any finite scalar matrix, let $n\in\mathbf N$ denote exponent $n+1$, and let $K\in D(B_n)$ be any derived object of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that the derived restriction of $K$ to $U$ is isomorphic to the constant cone of $\bar d:A_n^a\to A_n^b$. Then $H^{-1}(K)|_U\simeq\underline{\ker(\bar d)}|_U$, $H^0(K)|_U\simeq\underline{\operatorname{coker}(\bar d)}|_U$, and $H^i(K)|_U=0$ for $i\ne-1,0$. The same two isomorphisms hold for homology computed in the slice derived category. No scalar resolution, injectivity, local-model hypothesis, finite quotient ring, transition compatibility, or cover is assumed.

proof.text: The mapping cone of a scalar map between degree-zero finite free modules has homology its scalar kernel in degree -1, its scalar cokernel in degree 0, and zero elsewhere. The statement includes zero ranks.

Apply exact constant realization and exact slice restriction. They preserve kernels and cokernels, so give the same description for the restricted constant matrix complex. Exact slice restriction also commutes with homology, on complexes and after derived localization.

Apply the homology functors to the supplied derived isomorphism and compose with the homology localization comparison. The two constant homology descriptions give both the restricted global homology and the homology in the slice; all remaining degrees are zero.
